nodes.summary: Let $H$ be an abelian group of order $2^m$, let $n \ge 1$ and let $G = H \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$. Call an element of $G$ odd when its $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$-coordinate, taken as a representative in $\{0, 1, \dots, 2^n - 1\}$, is odd. Then the number of perfect covers of $G$ with exactly one odd element is $2^m \cdot 2^{n-1} \cdot C(H \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^{n-1}})$, where $C(K)$ denotes the number of perfect covers of a…
nodes.title: Perfect covers with exactly one odd element

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $2^n$ and $H$ a subgroup of order $2^m$. Then the number of perfect covers of $G$ that contain a perfect cover of $H$ is $2^{m(n-m)} \cdot C(G/H) \cdot C(H)$, where $C(K)$ denotes the number of perfect covers of a group $K$.
nodes.title: Perfect covers containing a perfect cover of a subgroup

nodes.summary: Write $C(K)$ for the number of perfect covers of a group $K$, and for natural numbers $m$ and $n$ let $b_{m,n} = C((\mathbb{Z}_2)^m \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n})$. Then: for every $m \ge 0$, $C((\mathbb{Z}_2)^m) \cdot m! = \prod_{i=0}^{m-1} (2^m - 2^i)$; for all $m, n \ge 1$, writing $B_{m,k} = 2^m \prod_{i=0}^{k-1} (2^m - 2^i) / (k+1)!$ for $1 \le k \le m$, we have…
nodes.title: Perfect covers of $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^m \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$

nodes.summary: Write $C(K)$ for the number of perfect covers of a group $K$. For every $n \ge 0$, $C((\mathbb{Z}_2)^2 \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}) = 2^{2n-2} \, 2^{n(n-1)/2} \, (3n^2 + 13n + 12)$ and $C((\mathbb{Z}_2)^3 \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}) = 2^{3n-3} \, 2^{n(n-1)/2} \, (28n^3 + 196n^2 + 392n + 224)$, where $2^{2n-2}$ and $2^{3n-3}$ are integer powers of $2$ (fractional at $n = 0$).
nodes.title: Perfect covers of an elementary abelian group of order 4 or 8 times a cyclic 2-group

nodes.summary: For a finite abelian group $G$, the number $C(G)$ of perfect covers of $G$ equals the number of elements of the finite set of all subsets of $G$ that are perfect covers.
nodes.title: Perfect cover count as a finset cardinality

nodes.summary: Writing $C(K)$ for the number of perfect covers of a group $K$, we have $C(\mathbb{Z}_2) = 1$, $C(\mathbb{Z}_4) = 2$ and $C(\mathbb{Z}_2 \oplus \mathbb{Z}_2) = 3$.
nodes.title: Small values of the perfect cover count

nodes.summary: Write $C(K)$ for the number of perfect covers of a group $K$, and $a_{m,n} = C(\mathbb{Z}_{2^m} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n})$. For all $m \ge n \ge 1$, $a_{m,n} = 2^{m+n-1} (a_{m-1,n} + 2 a_{m,n-1}) - 3 \cdot 2^{2m+2n-4} \, a_{m-1,n-1}$. Moreover, for every $n \ge 0$ there is a polynomial $p$ of degree $n$ with rational coefficients such that $a_{m,n} = 2^{(m-1)n} \, 2^{m(m-1)/2} \, p(m)$ for all $m \ge n$.
nodes.title: Perfect covers of a product of two cyclic 2-groups

nodes.summary: Write $C(K)$ for the number of perfect covers of a group $K$. For every $n \ge 0$, $C(\mathbb{Z}_{2^n} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_2) = 2^{n-1} \, 2^{n(n-1)/2} \, (n + 2)$, where $2^{n-1}$ is an integer power of $2$ (equal to $1/2$ at $n = 0$). For every $n \ge 1$, $C(\mathbb{Z}_{2^n} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_4) = 2^{2n-2} \, 2^{n(n-1)/2} \, (n^2 + 11n + 4)$. For every $n \ge 2$,…
nodes.title: Perfect covers of a cyclic 2-group times a cyclic group of order 2, 4 or 8

nodes.summary: For every $n \ge 0$, the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ has exactly $2^{n(n-1)/2}$ perfect covers.
nodes.title: Number of perfect covers of a cyclic 2-group

nodes.summary: For an abelian group $G$, $C(G)$ is the number of perfect covers of $G$: finite subsets $S \subseteq G$ such that every element of $G$ is the sum of exactly one subset of $S$ (the empty subset has sum $0$).
nodes.title: Number of perfect covers

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $s = (x_1, \dots, x_{k+1})$ be a family in $G$ that is a perfect $2^j$-cover of $G$, and let $S_1 = (x_1, \dots, x_k)$. For every $a \in G$, if $S_1$ covers $a$ exactly $c$ times, then $S_1$ covers $a + x_{k+1}$ exactly $2^j - c$ times.
nodes.title: Removing the last element of a perfect $2^j$-cover

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $s = (x_1, \dots, x_{k+1})$ be a family in $G$ that is a perfect $2^j$-cover of $G$, and let $S_1 = (x_1, \dots, x_k)$. For every $b \in G$, if $S_1$ covers $b$ exactly $c$ times, then for every integer $t$ it covers $b + 2t\,x_{k+1}$ exactly $c$ times and $b + (2t + 1)\,x_{k+1}$ exactly $2^j - c$ times.
nodes.title: Shifting by multiples of the last element of a perfect $2^j$-cover

nodes.summary:
Let $G$ be an abelian group, and for a finite set $A \subseteq G$ write $\mathcal{T}(A)$ for the set of odd combinations of $A$. Let $x = (x_1, \dots, x_m)$ be a family in $G$ such that $x_i 
otin \mathcal{T}(\{x_1, \dots, x_{i-1}\})$ for every $i$ (for $i = 1$ this says $x_1 
e 0$, and for $i \ge 2$ it forces $x_i 
e 0$). Then $x$ covers every element of $G$ at most once, that is, all subset sums of $x$ are…
nodes.title: Distinct subset sums from the odd-combination condition

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group, $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family in $G$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$ (a colored multiset), and $g \in G$. The cover count of $g$ by $s$ is the number of index sets $I \subseteq \iota$ with $\sum_{i \in I} s_i = g$: the number of times $s$ covers $g$ by its subset sums (the empty set covers $0$).
nodes.title: Cover count

nodes.summary: Let $m, n$ be natural numbers with $m + n > 0$. Every perfect cover of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^m} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ contains an element of order $2$.
nodes.title: Elements of order $2$ in perfect covers of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^m} \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite abelian group of order $2^m$, let $n \ge 1$, and let $G = H \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$. For every $k$ with $1 \le k \le m + 1$, some perfect cover $S$ of $G$ has exactly $k$ elements $(h, y)$ whose coordinate $y \in \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ is odd.
nodes.title: Perfect covers with a prescribed number of odd last coordinates

nodes.summary: Every finite abelian group $G$ of order $2^n$ has a perfect cover, and every nonzero $x \in G$ lies in some perfect cover of $G$.
nodes.title: Existence of perfect covers

nodes.summary: Let $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$ (a colored multiset). Then $s$ is a perfect $m$-cover of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ for some $m$ if and only if for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ some $s_i$ has additive order $2^j$.
nodes.title: Which families are perfect $m$-covers of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$

nodes.summary: Let $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$. If $s$ is a perfect $m$-cover of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$, then there is a finite set $T \subseteq \iota$ such that the subfamily $(s_i)_{i \in T}$ is a perfect $1$-cover of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$.
nodes.title: Perfect $m$-covers of $\mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ contain perfect covers

nodes.summary: Let $H$ be a finite abelian group of order $2^r$ and let $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ be a family in $H \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ indexed by a finite type $\iota$. If $s$ is a perfect $m$-cover of $H \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$, then for every $j$ with $1 \le j \le n$ the second coordinate of some $s_i$ has additive order $2^j$.
nodes.title: Orders of second coordinates in perfect $m$-covers

nodes.summary: In the cyclic group $\mathbb{Z}_4 = \mathbb{Z}/4\mathbb{Z}$, the set $\{1, 2\}$ is a perfect cover and the set $\{1, 3\}$ is not, since $1 + 3 = 0$.
nodes.title: Perfect covers of ℤ₄: an example and a non-example

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group. A finite set $S \subseteq G$ is a perfect cover of $G$ when every element of $G$ is the sum of exactly one subset of $S$ (the empty subset has sum $0$); that is, the family of the elements of $S$ is a perfect $1$-cover of $G$.
nodes.title: Perfect cover

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group, let $k$ and $N$ be natural numbers, and let $a, b, s_1, \dots, s_N \in G$. If the family $(a, s_1, \dots, s_N)$ is a perfect $2^k$-cover of $G$ and $b = (2j + 1)a$ for some integer $j$, then the family $(b, s_1, \dots, s_N)$ is also a perfect $2^k$-cover of $G$.
nodes.title: Replacing an entry of a perfect $2^k$-cover by an odd multiple

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group and let $s = (s_1, \dots, s_k)$ be a perfect $m$-cover of $G$. For every $g \in G$, the family $(g, s_1, \dots, s_k)$ is a perfect $2m$-cover of $G$.
nodes.title: Adjoining an element doubles the multiplicity of a perfect cover

nodes.summary: Let $H$ and $K$ be finite abelian groups with $|H| = 2^m$ and $|K| = 2^n$, and let $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$, indexed by a finite set $\iota$, be a perfect $l$-cover of $H \oplus K$. Then the first coordinates of the $s_i$ form a perfect $2^n l$-cover of $H$, and the second coordinates form a perfect $2^m l$-cover of $K$.
nodes.title: Projections of a perfect cover of a direct sum

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group, $m$ a natural number and $s = (s_i)_{i \in \iota}$ a family of elements of $G$ indexed by a finite set $\iota$ (a colored multiset: repeated values count separately). The family $s$ is a perfect $m$-cover of $G$ when every $g \in G$ equals $\sum_{i \in I} s_i$ for exactly $m$ subsets $I \subseteq \iota$ (the empty subset has sum $0$).
nodes.title: Perfect $m$-cover

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group and $A$ a finite subset of $G$, and let $\mathcal{T}(A)$ be the set of combinations $\sum_{y \in A} c_y y$ in which every integer coefficient $c_y$ is $0$ or odd. Every $x \in A$ lies in $\mathcal{T}(A)$: take $c_x = 1$ and $c_y = 0$ for $y \neq x$.
nodes.title: Elements of a finite set are odd combinations of it

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $2^n$, let $S$ be a perfect cover of $G$, and let $A \subseteq S$ contain no element of order $2$. Let $\mathcal{T}(A)$ be the set of combinations $\sum_{x \in A} c_x x$ in which every integer coefficient $c_x$ is $0$ or odd. Then $\mathcal{T}(A)$ does not contain exactly one element of order $2$: it contains none or at least two.
nodes.title: Elements of order two among odd combinations of part of a perfect cover

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group and, for a finite $A \subseteq G$, let $\mathcal{T}(A)$ be the set of combinations $\sum_{x \in A} c_x x$ in which every integer coefficient $c_x$ is $0$ or odd. Then $\mathcal{T}(\emptyset) = \{0\}$.
nodes.title: Odd combinations of the empty set

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be an abelian group of order $2^n$ and $S$ a perfect cover of $G$. For a finite $A \subseteq G$, let $\mathcal{T}(A)$ be the set of combinations $\sum_{x \in A} c_x x$ in which every integer coefficient $c_x$ is $0$ or odd. Then: (a) for disjoint $A, B \subseteq S$, $\mathcal{T}(A) \cap \mathcal{T}(B) = \{0\}$; (b) if $A \subseteq S$ and $s \in S \setminus A$, then $s \notin \mathcal{T}(A)$.
nodes.title: Odd combinations of disjoint parts of a perfect cover

nodes.summary: For a finite subset $A$ of an abelian group $G$, $\mathcal{T}(A)$ is the set of all sums $\sum_{x \in A} c_x x$ with integer coefficients $c_x$ such that every $c_x$ is either $0$ or odd.
nodes.title: Odd combinations

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $2^n$ and let $a, b \in G$ be nonzero. Then $b = (2j+1)a$ for some integer $j$ if and only if, for every perfect cover $S$ of $G$ with $a \in S$, the set $(S \setminus \{a\}) \cup \{b\}$ is again a perfect cover of $G$. If moreover $a \ne b$, then $b = (2j+1)a$ for some integer $j$ if and only if no perfect cover of $G$ contains both $a$ and $b$.
nodes.title: Odd multiples and replacement in perfect covers

nodes.summary: Let $G$ be a finite abelian group of order $2^n$, let $S$ be a perfect cover of $G$, let $z \in S$ and let $S_1 = S \setminus \{z\}$. Then (a) every element of $G$ is the sum of at most one subset of $S_1$, and exactly half of the $2^n$ elements of $G$ are the sum of a subset of $S_1$; (b) if $g \in G$ is the sum of a subset of $S_1$ and $j$ is an integer with $j \ge 1$, then $g + 2jz$ is the sum of a subset of…
nodes.title: Removing one element from a perfect cover

nodes.summary: Let $s = (s_1, \dots, s_{m+n})$, $s_i = (x_i, y_i)$, be a family in $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^m \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ that is a perfect $1$-cover: every element of the group is the sum of the $s_i$ over exactly one set of indices. Let $k + 1 \le m + n$ and suppose that $y_i$, read as an integer in $\{0, \dots, 2^n - 1\}$, is odd exactly when $i \le k + 1$. Let $V$ be the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-span of $x_{k+2}, \dots, x_{m+n}$ in…
nodes.title: The even tail of a perfect cover

nodes.summary: Let $m$, $n$ and $k$ be natural numbers with $k + 1 \le m + n$, and let $s = (s_1, \dots, s_{m+n})$, $s_i = (x_i, y_i)$, be a family in $(\mathbb{Z}_2)^m \oplus \mathbb{Z}_{2^n}$ that is a perfect $1$-cover: every element of the group is the sum of the $s_i$ over exactly one set of indices. Suppose that $y_i$, read as an integer in $\{0, \dots, 2^n - 1\}$, is odd exactly when $i \le k + 1$. Let $U$ be the…
nodes.title: Spans of the odd and even entries of a perfect cover

nodes.summary: For every finite subset $A$ of an abelian group $G$, $0$ lies in the set $\mathcal{T}(A)$ of odd combinations of $A$ (take every coefficient equal to $0$).
nodes.title: Zero is an odd combination

nodes.summary: Let $A$ be a finite subset of an abelian group $G$. If $g$ lies in the set $\mathcal{T}(A)$ of odd combinations of $A$, then $(2j+1)g \in \mathcal{T}(A)$ for every integer $j$.
nodes.title: Odd combinations are closed under odd multiples

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
